Article Title: Translating the Reliance ethos into a blueprint for nation-building
Article Text:
Translating familial empathy into enterprise resilience

Democratising technology for a billion aspirations

Reclaiming soft power and passing the baton

There is a prevailing wisdom in global business schools that suggests the larger an enterprise grows, the colder it must become. Scale, the theory goes, demands a clinical detachment. Yet, in the heart of India's corporate landscape, a remarkably different experiment has been playing out for decades. Here, the traditional Indian family ethos has not been discarded as an archaic social structure but rather leveraged as a sophisticated business strategy.The recently released Reliance documentary, 'Parvah Hai Toh Parivar Hai', pulls back the curtain on this machinery. It offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands, and ultimately to a nation of 1.4 billion people.Stripping away the complex financial jargon often associated with India's largest enterprise, the film reveals a foundational philosophy rooted in care, trust, and self-reliance. It asks a compelling question: can familial empathy actually drive a nation's socio-economic trajectory?At the corporate level, this paternalistic model is far more than a warm metaphor. It operates as a highly effective structural framework. The fundamental premise that care defines a family dictates how the company handles its human capital. During moments of intense crisis, such as health emergencies or natural disasters, this responsibility translates into the swift mobilisation of healthcare, isolation facilities, and emergency resources.This culture of protective support builds a rare institutional resilience, fostering a fiercely loyal ecosystem. Recalling the early days of setting up Jio Studios, an executive describes the deep personal involvement of the leadership. "I remember Mukesh Bhai and Manoj Bhai laying out their vision for the media business," she notes. "I remember thinking, do I have to pay to work here because this kind of mentorship is something that money cannot buy. "When creative and professional ventures face unexpected headwinds, this cushion of corporate confidence remains largely intact. Actor Ranveer Singh, reflecting on his collaborations with the conglomerate, highlighted this unusual patience. "I was given all the love, all the support and all the encouragement even at a time when my movies were not doing well," he shares in the film. "Career ups and downs. But to have received that kind of support meant a lot to me. It's nothing short of a blessing, an honour and a privilege to be associated with the Ambani family."However, the true test of any family-led business model lies in its ability to step outside its own perimeter and serve the wider community. For Reliance, modern nation building has meant translating massive corporate capacity into accessible public utility. Having already rewired India's digital landscape by making high-speed data universal through Jio, the enterprise is now looking towards the next frontier.The leadership frequently questions how their scale affects the masses. According to the documentary, the next step involves using new age technologies to bridge socio-economic gaps. "How does it affect the 1.4 billion people of India as we democratise information," the film asks, noting that generative artificial intelligence is "now democratising intelligence amongst 1.4 billion people."The ambition is to create tools that serve every stratum of society. The narrative paints a stark rural reality, envisioning a person in Bhagalpur "able to really use an AI tutor to teach himself or a farmer who is able to really understand what his food productivity would be." As the leadership points out, with this knowledge, "he is able to think more, he is able to do more, he is able to earn more and that is I think the ultimate goal for us. "Recognising that there are many Indias cutting across different income classes, the company is pivoting toward voice-first interfaces designed for the country's vast linguistic diversity. The documentary rightly points out that "Indians actually converse with technology by voice first rather than text." It is framed as a massive opportunity "which truly only an Indian company can solve." This ethos of mass accessibility comes directly from the top. As Mukesh Ambani directed his team regarding their massive streaming footprint: "The business is always important but I want consumers to experience our innovation."Beyond digital infrastructure, nation building requires fierce cultural stewardship. This household-led framework views corporate success as a catalyst for preserving national identity. Noting that foreign companies have historically dominated the sector, the documentary asserts, "There was no reason why an Indian company should not be leading the charts on media."Through Jio Studios, the mandate is bold: "What we want to do is claim back the narrative of India, especially young India." By backing massive commercial cinema alongside globally recognised projects, the conglomerate is actively shaping India's cultural footprint. Furthermore, spaces like the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre serve a dual purpose. "The vision of Mrs. Ambani and the vision of our centre is bringing the best of the world to India and the best of India to the world," the film notes.As the company approaches its 50th year, it stands at a critical juncture. Mukesh Ambani frames this generational shift not as a standard corporate handover, but as a continuation of core values. "Akash, Isha and Anant are only representatives of the young leaders," he explains. "And they will take our values. They will build an India of our dreams."At its heart, the enterprise remains anchored by its dining table roots. "To me, family is everything. I feel privileged that four generations of our family live together," shares Nita Ambani. This restless drive is perhaps best captured by 88-year-old V. Balasubramanian, who has spent 62 years at Reliance. He shares, "When I go away from this world, Dhirubhai is waiting there. We will start another Reliance Industries there and start working there and building up another empire. "Ultimately, the Reliance narrative suggests that India's economic rise is deeply intertwined with business models that align commercial scale with societal care. By treating a nation as an extended family, the company offers a compelling, distinctly Indian blueprint for modern nation building.
Article Summary: Reliance documentary 'parvah hai toh parivar hai' offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands. For reliance, modern nation building has meant translating massive corporate capacity into accessible public utility.

Article Title: Porn ads on FB, Insta lure users into fraud: Centre
Article Text:
NCTAU warns of financial fraud via malicious apps disguised as porn apps that take control of devices.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics unit (NCTAU), under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), has warned users of financial fraud through sideloaded malicious Android apps masquerading as porn apps which, when downloaded, take control of users’ devices by abusing accessibility permissions.NCTAU said misleading Facebook and Instagram ads under the names Night Play, Reloop, Kyss, Riva, Vima, Nexo and Vixa were redirecting users to phishing websites featuring pornographic content, with a prompt to download the APK file from outside the Google Play Store. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional applications, enabling fraudsters to take control of the device and commit financial fraud.Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route internet traffic pertaining to criminal activity. The app may prevent users from uninstalling it through device settings.Advisory asked users to install apps only from Play Store or trusted stores.
Article Summary: Nctau warns of financial fraud via malicious apps disguised as porn apps that take control of devices. Misleading facebook and instagram ads under the names night play, reloop, kyss, riva, vima, nexo and vixa were redirecting users to phishing websites featuring pornographic content.

Article Title: IISc sets up quantum computing hub under National Quantum Mission
Article Text:
The new Section 8 company will serve as the Quantum Computing Thematic Hub at IISc under the Union Govt’s National Quantum Mission

BENGALURU: IISc has set up a not-for-profit company to help build India’s capabilities in quantum computing, a technology expected to play a role in areas ranging from scientific research and industry to computing and communications in the coming years.Called the Foundation for QC Innovation (FQCI), the new Section 8 company will serve as the Quantum Computing Thematic Hub at IISc under the Union Govt’s National Quantum Mission.It’s one of four thematic hubs set up under the mission and will bring together researchers, academic institutions, industry and startups to develop quantum computing technologies in India.Quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process certain kinds of information differently from conventional computers. While the technology is still at an early stage, countries and companies around the world are investing heavily in it because of its potential to solve some problems that are difficult for existing computers.At IISc, the new hub will work across several approaches to building quantum computers, including systems based on light particles, superconducting circuits, semiconductor devices, neutral atoms and trapped ions.It will also work on quantum algorithms.“The National Quantum Mission provides a unique opportunity to build a strong and globally competitive quantum computing ecosystem in India. Our focus is on bringing together India’s research capabilities, advanced infrastructure, industry and entrepreneurial talent to translate cutting-edge research into indigenous quantum computing technologies and applications,” Shankar Kumar Selvaraja, project director, FQCI and professor, Centre for Nano Science and Engineering at IISc, said.A major part of the initiative will be the creation of shared facilities for making, testing and characterising quantum devices. The aim is to give researchers and companies access to infrastructure that can help move laboratory research towards working technologies.“FQCI will also focus on building the workforce and startup ecosystem required for the sector. Its programmes will support student research and internships, industry-academia collaboration, startup development and knowledge-sharing. The initiative has launched programmes called QC Rise, QC Bridge, QC Leap, QC Accel and QC Quest as part of these efforts,” IISc said.The larger goal, it added, was to reduce dependence on overseas technology by developing quantum computing capabilities within the country.
Article Summary: The new section 8 company will serve as the quantum computing thematic hub at iisc under the union govt’s national quantum mission.quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process certain kinds of information differently from conventional computers.

Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Samudra manthan is a rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in india’s offshore basins. The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks.

Article Title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
Article Text:
The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective. (PTI photo)

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.
Article Summary: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of sumb in j&k’s samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated. Article Title: In 1998, Steve Jobs convinced a 37-year-old Tim Cook to join near-bankrupt Apple, here's the 'story' he told to make him leave world's biggest PC company
Article Text:
When Steve Jobs convinced a 37-year-old Tim Cook to join near-bankrupt Appl

Steve Jobs’ vision of the iMac G3

Tim Cook ignored ‘career advice’ from peers

Apple hired Tim Cook in March 1998

Tim Cook concluded his 15-year tenure as Apple ’s CEO on August 31, 2026, transitioning to executive chairman of the board effective September 1, 2026. John Ternus, formerly senior vice president of hardware engineering, has officially taken the helm of the company. While Cook leaves behind an era defined by monumental commercial success, his beginnings at the company were far more modest. Back in early 1998, Apple was on the edge of financial collapse, struggling with plunging staff morale, and widely viewed as an undesirable employer across Silicon Valley. Yet, Steve Jobs managed to convince a 37-year-old rising executive to walk away from Compaq, which was then the global leader in personal computer sales, and join the struggling company.Before making the leap, Cook had built an extensive corporate resume, spending 12 years at IBM alongside key executive roles at Intelligent Electronics and Compaq. While Cook had repeatedly rejected outreach from Apple's recruitment team, he eventually agreed to a face-to-face sit-down with Jobs. Cook later explained to Charlie Rose in 2014 that he felt compelled to meet the person who had essentially built the modern computing industry and was pursuing a distinctive vision.During their introductory discussion, Jobs reportedly laid out his roadmap to revitalise Apple, describing an upcoming computer concept designed to upend the entire PC landscape. CNBC reported that Jobs shared preliminary details of a hardware design unlike anything on the market. The concept later materialised as the iMac G3, the vibrant, translucent computer that turned designer Jony Ive into an industry star.Cook walked away from the encounter fascinated by the design and convinced that collaborating alongside Jobs would represent the privilege of a lifetime.Taking the role required Cook to defy the advice of his closest peers and all conventional logic. Reflecting on the decision during his 2010 Auburn University commencement address, Cook noted that any logical cost-benefit evaluation favoured staying at Compaq. One chief executive even warned Cook that leaving the market leader for Apple would be foolish.Cook believed that following the crowd was a mistake. Recognizing the deep operational challenges facing Apple, he decided he could make a meaningful impact and trusted his intuition over traditional career calculations.In March 1998, Jobs formally appointed Cook as senior vice president of worldwide operations, providing him a base compensation of $400,000 alongside a $500,000 signing bonus. Cook took charge of completely overhauling Apple’s supply chain, manufacturing systems and global distribution.Cook’s procurement and operations background proved to be an ideal match for Apple's recovery and for Jobs' management approach. Speaking to biographer Walter Isaacson for the book Steve Jobs, the late Apple co-founder reflected on their dynamic:“He had the same vision I did. We could interact at a high strategic level, and I could just forget about a lot of things unless he came and pinged me.”
Article Summary: Tim cook concluded his 15-year tenure as apple’s ceo on august 31, 2026. John ternus, formerly senior vice president of hardware engineering, has officially taken the helm of the company. Back in early 1998, apple was on the edge of financial collapse, struggling with plunging staff morale.

Article Title: Government sounds alarm, ads on Facebook ‌and Instagram found directing users to apps that steal banking passwords and remotely control users' phones
Article Text:
How these apps work, spy and steal

How to uninstall these apps

The government has warned of malicious porn apps on Instagram and Facebook that can completely take over Android phones. In an advisory, National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) said that it has observed a rise in financial frauds perpetrated through malicious Android apps masquerading as pornography apps, circulated through Facebook and Instagram ads. As per the Ministry of Home Affairs advisory, these Android apps are operating under the names "Night Play", "Reloop", "Kyss", “Vimo”, “Rivo”, “Nexo”, “Vixa” and other similar variants.These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content, where the user is prompted to download an APK file. After installation, the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional apps and by misusing accessibility permission, take control of the users’ device. Some apps also install a VPN, which may be used to route internet traffic pertaining to malicious/criminal activity. As per government warning, these apps can secretly access information stored on users' phones, capture one-time passwords and bank PINs, and transfer money from ​accounts without the owner's knowledge. Not just this, the apps also make it difficult for users to uninstall them through device's normal settings.Distribution: The malicious apps are distributed through pornographic content related advertisements or links majorly on Facebook and Instagram. These ads redirect to phishing websites.Redirection: Ads redirect to phishing websites serving pornographic content. Domains of the website majorly belong to “.live”. Users are persuaded to download and install the APK from sources outside the Google Play Store.App Update: A secondary package gets downloaded and installed on the pretext of an app update, based on permissions abused by the first, initial app.Abuse of Accessibility Permission for device takeover: After installation, the app asks users to grant Accessibility and other sensitive permissions. Once enabled, the malware gains control of the device and continues to run in the background.VPN Installation: Some apps may also install a VPN on the device, thereby routing all internet traffic through attacker-controlled servers. This compromises user's transmitted data, which may subsequently be exploited for malicious or criminal activities.Unauthorized Transactions: Since the malware has the ability to take over the compromised device, installing such apps may lead to financial fraud.METHOD 1: Safe Mode RebootStep 1: Start Your Phone in Safe Mode: Press and hold the Power button. Press and hold Power Off until the Safe Mode option appears. Click OK or Restart in Safe Mode. Wait for the phone to restart. "Safe Mode" will appear at the bottom of the screen.Step 2: Uninstall the App: Open Settings. Go to Apps. Select the suspicious application. Tap Uninstall. Remove any other unknown or related apps.Step 3: Restart Normally: Restart the phone. The device will exit Safe Mode automatically.Second MethodStep 1: Restore the Default Home Screen (If required): Open Settings. Go to Apps → Default Apps → Home App. Select your phone's original launcher (System Launcher, One UI Home, Pixel Launcher, etc.).Step 2: Disable Accessibility Access: Open Settings. Tap Accessibility. Open Installed Services or Downloaded Apps. Select the suspicious application. Turn Accessibility Off.Step 3: Remove Administrator Access: Open Settings. Go to Security or Security & Privacy.Open Device Admin Apps or Device Administrators. If the suspicious app is enabled, select it. Tap Deactivate or Turn Off.Verify the Device: Open Settings > Apps. Confirm that the suspicious application has been removed. If the app cannot be removed or returns after restarting, back up your important data and perform a Factory Reset.
Article Summary: The government has warned of malicious porn apps on instagram and facebook that can completely take over android phones. These apps are primarily distributed through advertisements on facebook and instagram, which redirect to websites and apps showing pornographic content.

Article Title: As Google renames 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US; company's 'update' on what users in the US, Canada and 'rest of the world' will see
Article Text:
Google statement on the name chang

Canada PM Mark Carney on US renaming the Lake Ontario

Trump sends direct message to Apple to change the name

Escalating the trade dispute with Canada, US President Donald Trump last week announced that he was changing the name of the smallest of the five Great Lakes. As the trade talks between the US and Canada broke down, leading to a wave of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'.After Trump's announcement, Google began rolling out this change for US users. The company posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps. This primarily means that the company has to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps. Google's update on the name change also made it clear that the change will be only for Google Map users in the US. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America'. Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see the 'Lake Ontario' label. In the rest of the world, Lake Ontario will take precedence, but Lake America will also be there in parentheses."The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States. Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S.,people using Maps in the U.S. will see "Lake America," those in Canada will continue to see "Lake Ontario," and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names. These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now," said the company in a blog update.In a post on X, formerly Twitter, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney wrote, "The name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means “the lake is beautiful, the lake is big”. The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America. We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms. Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario – then, now and always."President Trump has reportedly "reached out to Apple directly" about changing Lake Ontario's name to Lake America in Apple Maps. According to US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, “The president reached out to Apple directly, so I’m sure that we may be seeing that change coming up soon to Lake America.” Burgum shared the same in an ‌interview ⁠on Fox Business’ “Mornings with Maria” programme.

As the trade talks between the us and canada broke down, leading to a wave of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, trump signed an executive order to rename lake ontario to 'lake america' after trump's announcement, google began rolling out this change for us users.

Article Title: Elon Musk's $60 billion purchase of Cursor that has made Sam Altman 'upset' has an 'indian connection', Aman Sanger
Article Text:
Who is Aman Sanger

Who is Aman Sanger

SpaceX acquire Cursor

OpenAI ends relationship with Cursor

Elon Musk’s $60 billion acquisition of Cursor has put the AI coding startup and its co-founder Aman Sanger in the spotlight, with the deal also drawing attention in India because of Sanger’s family roots. Aman Sanger, who was born in the US to Indian immigrant parents, co-founded Cursor in 2022 after studying computer science at MIT. The AI coding company grew rapidly before being acquired by Musk’s SpaceX, with its founders reportedly receiving billions of dollars in SpaceX shares. The deal has also added another layer to Musk’s rivalry with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman who recently called off its partnership with Cursor.For the 26-year-old Sanger, however, the story goes beyond the Musk-Altman feud, with his Indian family background adding an unexpected connection to the blockbuster AI deal.Born in the US to Indian immigrant parents, Aman Sanger grew up in a household where academic achievement and business success were strongly encouraged. His father, Arvind Sanger, graduated from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay with a B. Tech degree in 1984 before moving to US. He later earned an MBA from Tulane University and built a successful career on Wall Street. His mother, Shilpa became an angel investor through the investment network Golden Seeds.She also took on a business management role at Geosphere Capital.Aman Sanger started coding at the age of 14 and developed an early interest in technology. After enrolling at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), he studied computer science between 2018 and 2022.Sanger cofounded Cursor, the maker of a popular AI code editing tool, with three friends from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 2022. Before starting his own company, Sanger gained experience through internships at Google and Bridgewater Associates. He also launched an AI consultancy before joining fellow MIT students Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark to create Cursor in 2022.According to Forbes latest estimate, Aman Sanger has a net worth of over $2.5 billion.Last month, the company was acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion. Forbes estimates that each Cursor cofounder received shares of the rocket maker worth $2.4 billion at the deal's closing.Before the SpaceX acquisition, Cursor claimed to have more than $1 billion in annualized revenue, making it one of the fastest growing AI startups. Today, millions of software developers at enterprises like Nvidia, Adobe, Uber, Shopify and PayPal use Cursor to generate and edit chunks of code.Last week, OpenAI pulled its models out of Cursor, with a proposed shutoff date of November 12, 2026. There is no dispute here about pricing, performance or usage limits. The stated reason is Elon Musk, and OpenAI put that in writing in a public blog post rather than letting it leak out through a support page.OpenAI claims that X, formerly Twitter and now folded into SpaceX, broke the terms of its contract after Musk took over the platform. It also points to sworn testimony this year in which Musk acknowledged that xAI, likewise now part of SpaceX, had violated OpenAI's terms of service. OpenAI added that its forthcoming model, Astra, raises the accountability bar further, which is why it would rather end the arrangement than extend it to a partner it does not trust. It says it gave the maximum notice its contract allows so developers get time to plan.
Article Summary: Aman sanger was born in the us to indian immigrant parents. He co-founded cursor, the maker of a popular ai code editing tool, with three friends from the massachusetts institute of technology in 2022. Forbes estimates that each cursor cofounder received shares of the rocket maker worth $2.4 billion at the deal's closing.

Article Title: OpenAI is touting ads as 'diversified business model' as it gears up for its massive IPO
Article Text:
OpenAI CEO Sam ​Altman

How OpenAI’s ad business started

Where Ads Are Rolling Out Now

OpenAI's guardrails on the Ads

What comes next

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI announced recently that its advertising business has reached a $1 billion annualised revenue rate, just 200 days after its launch, according to a report by CNBC. The company is positioning this milestone as a proof of its ‘diversified business model’ as it prepares for a massive initial public offering (IPO). OpenAI is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation to investors, with ads now joining enterprise offerings, consumer subscriptions, and usage-based APIs as key revenue streams.OpenAI started testing ads inside ChatGPT in the US back in February this year, a move that was both widely anticipated and genuinely controversial. Digital advertising has long served as the primary profit engine for other tech giants like Google and Meta, but OpenAI's entry into that space drew direct mockery from its chief rival, Anthropic, which built its first-ever Super Bowl ad campaign specifically around contrasting itself with OpenAI's ad push.ChatGPT Ads are now live in more than 40 countries, and OpenAI said Monday it's expanding self-service access to advertisers across India, Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa.Recently, the company also announced the launch ChatGPT Ads in India. The company has revealed that it is expanding its advertising program to one of ChatGPT’s largest and most active markets. The company confirmed that the ads will roll out to logged‑in adults using the Free and Go tiers, while Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Education subscriptions will remain ad‑free. WPP and Omnicom will be OpenAI’s first agency partners for ChatGPT Ads in India. With more than 50 brands set to go live this week, these agencies bring strong relationships across industries and expertise in strategy, creative, measurement, brand safety, and campaign execution. OpenAI said the model is non‑exclusive and it will continue to identify and work with other agencies.Within the chatbot, ads appear for users on OpenAI's Go subscription tier as well as its free tier — the free tier alone makes up the vast majority of ChatGPT's roughly 1 billion weekly active users, giving the ad business a massive built-in audience.OpenAI said its ads are clearly labeled and do not influence ChatGPT's actual answers to users. The company also said advertisers do not get access to users' private conversations, an apparent effort to get ahead of privacy concerns that have followed the rollout since its announcement in February.In a release, OpenAI said its next phase of growth will expand ChatGPT Ads into additional markets while introducing new ad formats, campaign objectives, buying options, and measurement tools for advertisers. The company also said it plans to explore new, more native ways for businesses to interact directly with consumers inside ChatGPT.
Article Summary: Chatgpt-maker openai announced recently that its advertising business has reached a $1 billion annualised revenue rate. The company is positioning this milestone as a proof of its ‘diversified business model’ as it prepares for a massive initial public offering (ipo)

Article Title: Top tech investor Gavin Baker regrets his comments on data centres; says what I should have said is: There are reasonable concerns and ...
Article Text:
Representative Image

Gavin Baker’s original post on data centers

The walkback

Addressing key issues

A revised stance

Read Gavin Baker’s complete post here

Regret the tone of my post on data centers yesterday.

What I should have said:

There were reasonable concerns about data centers 18ish months ago: water, taxes, jobs, electricity prices, the environment and what they would do to small towns.

Well-structured data center projects have largely addressed these concerns today and we should be celebrating this.

On balance, data centers are awesome for America in every way.

On water: U.S. data centers use a fraction of what golf courses use. A lot of the numbers from 18 months ago were off by over 1000x. Newer data centers use closed-loop systems or recycled water. Should be required by every town approving a data center project.

On taxes: looking only at sales-tax exemptions, as Ronan Farrow did, is the wrong way to evaluate this. Data centers pay significant property taxes. Loudoun County, which is the wealthiest county in America, now collects on the order of $1 billion a year from data centers. In Quincy, WA, data centers are more than half the property-tax roll. Over time, property taxes can go to zero while government spending increases in these towns.

On jobs: this has been unambiguously awesome for blue collar Americans. Demand for electricians, plumbers, welders, HVAC techs, and contractors has gone vertical, and it is not a one-time construction job. These buildings get upgraded and expanded over time. That is why the building trades are fighting for them, and why some unions are now treating opposition to data centers as a reason not to endorse politicians.

On power: the original fear was that households would pay for the incremental electricity demand in the form of higher prices. That is why the ratepayer-protection deals and the new large-load tariffs exist. The right structure is: the data center brings or pays for new generation and signs a contract long enough that existing customers are protected. Where that is happening, utilities are cutting or freezing residential rates and saying so on the record.

Where it is not, people are right to object. Electricity prices are going down *today* in a number of large states because of data centers.

On the environment: data centers overwhelming use natural gas today, which is the cleanest power source outside of nuclear, solar and wind. And the companies that are building the data centers are committed to carbon neutrality such that an equivalent amount of solar will likely be built.

Maybe more importantly, the data centers need batteries to function effectively and these batteries can also sell energy back into the grid (which recently prevented blackouts in Texas).

Over time, data centers will run on solar plus batteries.

On the towns: Poverty in Quincy, WA fell from 29% to 6%. Data center taxes paid for a new high school, a hospital, a library, police and fire stations. This is happening in many left for dead former mill and farm towns that had no other bidder for the land.

Data centers are actually reindustrializing parts of America and creating the kind of working-class jobs both parties have spent decades claiming to support. That should not be a partisan issue. Data centers can and should be awesome for America and they increasingly, overwhelmingly are. Supporting the outsourcing of data centers to China will likely age just as well as support for the outsourcing of high quality, blue collar manufacturing jobs to China has aged.

When the facts change, I change my mind. I hope that reasonable people who had good faith reasons to oppose data centers at least consider updating their beliefs given the change in the facts over the last 18 months. This really matters for America.

I will say I also think the idea of making data centers beautiful is a good one that has yet to be implemented. Data centers should be just as beautiful as Grand Central Station. We can learn a lot from the railroad buildout. Neoclassical revival ftw.

Might write up open-weight AI tomorrow as this is equally essential to America.

Top tech investor Gavin Baker has publicly expressed regret over his earlier remakes dismissing opposition to data centers. In a post last week, Baker had written that ‘any politician opposed to data centers is unqualified to hold public office’, calling them a godsend for blue-collar workers and small towns. However, now Baker struck a a different tone, saying he regretted the phrasing and acknowledged that there were “reasonable concerns” about data centers around 18 months ago.Baker's earlier post declared that "nature is healing" on the data center debate, going as far as saying any politician opposed to data centers was unqualified to hold public office. In that post, he argued data centers were revitalizing small towns across America, delivering major benefits to blue-collar workers, lowering electricity costs, accelerating the shift to sustainable energy, and using only negligible amounts of water.In a follow-up post, Baker said he regretted the tone of his prior comments, offering a more measured version of his argument instead. He acknowledged that concerns about data centers were reasonable roughly 18 months ago, spanning issues like water usage, taxes, job creation, electricity prices, environmental impact, and effects on small towns. His revised position is that well-structured data center projects have since largely addressed those concerns, and that the industry's overall record now deserves to be seen as a positive for the country.Baker outlined how well-structured projects have since addressed worries over water usage, taxes, jobs, electricity prices, and environmental impact:•Water: U.S. data centers use far less water than golf courses, with newer facilities adopting closed-loop or recycled systems.•Taxes: While sales-tax exemptions drew criticism, Baker noted that property taxes from data centers have become a major revenue source in counties like Loudoun, VA and Quincy, WA.•Jobs: Demand for electricians, plumbers, welders, and HVAC technicians has surged, with unions now backing data center projects.•Power: Ratepayer-protection deals and large-load tariffs ensure households aren’t burdened by higher electricity costs. In some states, utilities have cut or frozen residential rates due to data center investments.•Environment: Facilities increasingly rely on natural gas, solar, and batteries, with commitments to carbon neutrality. Batteries also support grid stability, as seen in Texas.Impact on small townsBaker highlighted the transformation of towns like Quincy, WA, where poverty fell from 29% to 6% and tax revenues funded schools, hospitals, and libraries. He argued that data centers are “reindustrializing parts of America” and creating durable working-class jobs.Concluding his post, Baker said: “When the facts change, I change my mind. I hope that reasonable people who had good faith reasons to oppose data centers at least consider updating their beliefs given the change in the facts over the last 18 months.” He added that future projects should also focus on aesthetics, suggesting data centers be designed as beautifully as Grand Central Station.
Article Summary: There were reasonable concerns about data centers 18ish months ago: water, taxes, jobs, electricity prices, the environment and what they would do to small towns. Well-structured data center projects have largely addressed these concerns today. On balance, data centers are awesome for america in every way.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:

Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. Article Title: Meet Aditi Paudel, a 17-year-old high school student appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador
Article Text: Born in Japan, and raised in Nepal during her early childhood, Aditi Paudel had always shown an affinity towards reading. Her earliest memory of reading is of her grandfather handing her a newspaper filled with intricate Devanagari script when she was still in preschool. But to the surprise of those around her, she was still able to make sense of the text. Over the years, she has only improved and the now 17-year-old high school senior in Tokyo was recently appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador, as per a report by The Japan Times.The World Literacy Foundation, a global nonprofit headquartered in Australia is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating. While the program has been running for 12 years, this is the first time an ambassador from Japan has been appointed, according to Andrew Kay, CEO and founder of the World Literacy Foundation.The aim of the program is to connect young people around the world and get them “involved and waving the flag for literacy in their community,” Kay said, noting that Paudel was singled out “for her leadership, passion for literacy, and commitment to empowering young people in Japan.”“Her curiosity about English shaped thoughtful advocacy, strengthening the program’s global voice and cultural reach,” he added.Paudel returned to Japan to enter the third grade and along with settling into a new life, she found herself having to learn Japanese once more, which meant turning to the books. Her love for reading came pretty early in her life, nurtured by her father who bought her plenty of books. She developed an early taste for fantasy, and recalled falling in love with Enid Blyton’s “The Wishing-Chair.”Reading Malala Yousafzai 's autobiography, 'I Am Malala', helped her develop significant interests in female empowerment, including ensuring that women across the world have access to education and literacy. Along with working with children with disabilities, she plans to work with the Shanti Volunteer Association to collect and donate books to Asian countries with lower rates of literacy, including Nepal.With enough experience developing her own reading skills, Paudel said that a common view of literacy is how well a person can read or write, but she sees it in broader terms. Essentially, it’s “something that helps you open doors for more opportunities,” she noted.Paudel has experienced the impact of her access to private education firsthand and how it has set her life on a different course. “My parents grew up in a completely opposite environment. They did not have a childhood like this,” she said. “Being literate is so important because even though you have the potential, you can never unlock it if you do not have literacy.”But even those with easy access to books are reading less than they once did. Around half of elementary, junior high and high school age children in Japan do not read books, according to a recent study by Benesse Educational Research & Development Institute and the University of Tokyo.Fewer young people are reading for pleasure and enjoyment, said Kay, and that could cause a significant regressive effect. “As far as embedding themselves in a novel or reading something that really takes a little bit more effort, that is becoming a rarer thing,” he said. Kay also cautions against the impact of artificial intelligence, noting that the latest tech tools provide quick answers, allowing people to skip the process of researching, reading and wrestling with theories and thoughts oneself.“It’s turning our clock back 150 years … where most people couldn’t read or would have limited ability to read,” he said of the absence of reading books as a mainstream pursuit. Those trends only add importance to initiatives like the World Literacy Foundation’s ambassador program.As a teenager, Paudel understands growing up in a world full of distractions, where much of life is on and from social media. “You will always be more inclined to go for your phone rather than a book,” she said, and because of this, making reading a habit is critical. Her advice for developing a love of reading isn’t about ticking classics off a book list, but finding something that resonates, and that, ideally, can broaden the reader’s perspective.
Article Summary: Aditi paudel, a 17-year-old high school senior in tokyo, was recently appointed as japan's first literacy ambassador. The world literacy foundation is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating. This is the first time an ambassador from japan has been appointed.

Article Title: ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules
Article Text:
ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules﻿

ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it Monday to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny, a first for an AI chatbot.Brussels also designated Reddit and Roblox as “very large” online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight. “ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the EU, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society,” EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen said.The designation applies to platforms and search engines with over 45 million monthly active users in the 27-nation bloc, a threshold the three platforms reported meeting, the commission said. The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the Digital Services Act, a content law the EU has deployed to rein in Big Tech.
Article Summary: Chatgpt is first ai chatbot to face tougher eu rules. Reddit and roblox also designated as ‘very large’ online platforms. The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the digital services act.

Article Title: US states, consumer watchdog file lawsuit against Amazon for manipulating advertising prices
Article Text:
The company's shares reportedly fell 2.5 per cent after the lawsuit was announced.

US consumer watchdog, Federal Trade Commission (FTC), and a group of 22 US states filed a lawsuit against Amazon on Monday, accusing the company of overcharging its advertising customers by manipulating the online auctions that set ad prices.The company's shares reportedly fell 2.5 per cent after the lawsuit was announced.Amazon has gained nearly $20 billion from over a million advertising customers since 2019, the FTC and states allege in the lawsuit.According to a filed complaint reported by the BBC, "Amazon overrides and replaces the actual auction results with higher prices set by Amazon to increase its profits.""Consumers are suffering, have suffered, and will continue to suffer substantial injury as a result", it said."The FTC wants the public to believe this case is about higher prices for consumers. It is not," Amazon said in its statement.In a statement to the BBC, the company said it "strongly disagrees" with the premise of the lawsuit and called it "misguided".The FTC and the states also alleged that Amazon's practices have harmed consumers, as the additional advertising costs are ultimately passed on to shoppers.On Amazon's e-commerce platform, brands and sellers compete to place Sponsored Product and Sponsored Brands ads when consumers search for products using keywords.These ad placements are then auctioned to the highest bidder.The complaint alleges that Amazon secretly charged advertisers more through so-called "second price" auctions. Under this system, advertisers expect to pay one cent more than the next-highest bidder for each auction they win.However, the complaint alleges that Amazon charged Sponsored Products advertisers their own winning bid nearly 80 per cent of the time.The lawsuit said Amazon's practices were driven by its dissatisfaction with the revenue generated through its advertising auctions.Amazon said the FTC "fundamentally misunderstands how advertisers operate"."Advertisers adjust bids based on real-world performance, not descriptions of auction mechanics," the company said.Amazon added that average winning bids fell 50 per cent between 2019 and 2025 for Sponsored Products search ads. It also said roughly 92 per cent of placed ads are not awarded to the highest bidder.Notably, Amazon has faced legal action from the FTC in the past.Last year, the company settled a case brought by the FTC, which alleged that it had enrolled millions of consumers in its Prime subscription service without their consent and knowingly made it difficult for them to cancel.Amazon agreed to pay $2.5 billion to settle the case, including civil penalties and refunds to consumers.

Article Title: A Guatemalan immigrant began delivering pizzas in Dallas in 1987; decades later she built a franchise training organisation

Why Aicha Bascaro says franchisors teach the brand but not the business

How the academy's three programs serve different levels of a franchise organisation

What Bascaro built beyond the academy's formal programs

What comes next for the American Franchise Academy after 10 years

Aicha Bascaro arrived in the United States as an immigrant from Guatemala and, in 1987, took a job delivering pizzas at a Domino's restaurant in Dallas, Texas. What began as an entry-level job became the starting point for a career spanning more than three decades and almost every level of the franchise industry. Bascaro worked as a crew member and manager before moving into senior positions, including director of operations, vice president, international consultant and eventually brand president, where she oversaw more than 300 locations across the country. Along the way, she saw a gap that she believed was easy to overlook: franchise owners could be taught how to operate a particular brand without necessarily receiving the broader business education needed to lead and grow a company. That idea eventually became the foundation for the American Franchise Academy. In 2016, a struggling franchisee contacted Bascaro looking for help with a failing business, and instead of simply offering informal advice, she developed a structured training program around the problems he was facing. The American Franchise Academy was founded on July 18, 2016, and a decade later has grown into a specialised organisation focused on business management education for franchisees and their teams.According to the International Franchise Association, Bascaro created the academy around what she considers one of the franchise industry's biggest gaps. Franchisors generally provide extensive training on their own brands, teaching new owners how their particular systems work and how to operate according to established standards. Bascaro's view is that this brand-specific training does not necessarily cover the wider business skills required to lead and grow a franchise. She has described the distinction simply: franchisors provide the brand and train franchisees to operate it, but they cannot provide the broader business acumen. That, she says, is where the American Franchise Academy comes in, offering training focused on helping franchisees become stronger business leaders rather than simply better operators of a particular brand.The idea came from Bascaro's own experience in the industry. Having progressed from delivering pizzas to senior leadership roles, she had spent years seeing how responsibilities changed as people moved from working inside individual locations to managing larger operations. By the time the struggling franchisee contacted her in 2016, she had accumulated the practical experience to recognise that his problem was not necessarily a lack of effort or knowledge about the brand itself. He needed a more structured understanding of how to manage the business. That first training program eventually became the starting point for an academy built around a much broader idea: franchise ownership requires more than knowing the rules of the brand.The American Franchise Academy now divides its main curriculum into three programs designed for different levels of responsibility within a franchise organisation.MANAGE provides business-management education for single-unit franchisees and unit managers. The program is aimed at people responsible for the performance of an individual location and focuses on giving them a structured foundation in franchise business management.LEAD is designed for district managers, who oversee multiple locations and therefore operate at a different level from managers responsible for a single unit. The academy offers certification through the program, reflecting the additional responsibilities involved in managing teams and operations across several locations.At the top of the academy's structure is COMMAND, its flagship program. It brings together the broader curriculum intended for franchisees who want to lead and grow their businesses. The three-level structure allows the academy to address people at different stages of the franchise hierarchy rather than treating every operator as though they face the same challenges.Over its first decade, the academy says it has certified more than 400 district managers, more than 200 unit managers and around 100 franchisees. Its participants have come from some of the biggest names in franchising, including McDonald's, Popeyes, Dairy Queen, Subway, Dunkin' and Anytime Fitness. Those numbers also illustrate how the academy has moved beyond the single franchisee whose problems inspired Bascaro to create the original training program. What began as an attempt to help one struggling business has developed into a formal education system serving franchise professionals across multiple major brands.Bascaro's work has expanded beyond classroom-style certification. During the academy's first decade, she also built a wider collection of educational material around franchise management, including three Amazon bestselling books and a weekly blog focused on franchising and business education. She also hosts the Franchise Success Formulas podcast, which has attracted more than 19,000 YouTube subscribers. Together, the books, blog, podcast and certification programs have allowed the academy to reach people at different stages of their franchise careers and through different formats.Bascaro has also received recognition within the franchise industry. Her honours include being named to Nation's Restaurant News' 2022 Power List and receiving a Trailblazer Award. She also serves as a Certified Franchise Executive instructor for the International Franchise Association. The broader body of work reflects the same distinction that shaped the academy from the beginning. Bascaro's focus is not simply on teaching franchisees how to follow the operating model of a particular company. Instead, the academy treats business management as a separate area of education that franchise operators can continue developing throughout their careers. That distinction becomes particularly important when a franchisee grows. Running one location and leading a larger franchise operation involve different levels of responsibility, and the academy's programs are structured around those different stages.The academy is now looking beyond its first decade and toward expanding the reach of its training. One of its priorities is developing multilingual programs that could make the academy's business-management education available to franchise operators around the world rather than primarily serving English-speaking participants. The organisation is also expanding its work directly with franchisors. Through its franchisor partnership strategy, the academy aims to help individual brands provide structured business-management education to their franchise networks through an outside training organisation. Instead of requiring franchisees to find this kind of education independently, the model would allow brands to make it part of the wider support available to their operators.
